As I strolled through the lively streets, I overheard a group of settlers discussing their plans to expand into neighboring territories. The foreign diplomats seemed focused on some important matters concerning international trade and diplomacy, oblivious to the simmering tensions among the local populace.

items.text: Today, I sat in my makeshift office overlooking the lush Brazilian Amazon. The air was thick with the scent of eucalyptus and rainforest, a stark contrast to the White House news swirling in the skies above. President von der Leyen's words echoed through the valley – her support for Ukraine seemed distant now, overshadowed by the US relationship's decline. As I watched deforestation levels drop to their lowest ever, there was an eerie silence over the region, punctuated only by the occasional call of a macaw in protest. The future felt uncertain, like a whisper in this vast, almost silent expanse.

Suddenly, the serene silence was shattered by the announcement about von der Leyen’s support for Ukraine in The Guardian World. It felt like a reminder of the world's many crises, especially as I read about Katie Zacharia transitioning out at the White House. Outside my window, Brazil’s Amazon deforestation reached its lowest point on record, yet even here, there were signs that change was possible.
